inclusions: rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm, identified by EDX analysis

source.reason: The monocrystals (including the Fe-17%Al as-grown monocrystal) contained rare globular AlN inclusions up to 30 µm identified by EDX.
The alloy is a binary Fe-Al solid solution; the paper describes these Fe-Al alloys as bcc alloys with disordered/K-state structure depending on Al content (Fe-17%Al is in the K-state range).
The Fe-17%Al material of this sample is a monocrystal grown by the Bridgman method; as-grown monocrystals showed no carbides, and the only second-phase features were rare globular AlN inclusions.

overall_structure.value: Single crystal (monocrystal), as-grown; Fe-Al solid-solution matrix with rare globular AlN inclusions. No second-phase carbides present because no heat treatment was applied.

source.reason: Overall microstructural description of the as-grown Fe-17%Al monocrystal: single crystal with rare AlN inclusions and no carbides absent heat treatment.

unmapped_findings: The heat-treated variant of the Fe-17%Al monocrystal (with 70 ppm C) — 14 days at 320 °C with concurrent 100 MPa loading in <111> direction — contained thin carbides; without loading much less carbides were observed. This finding concerns a heat-treated condition and does NOT apply to the as-grown sample extracted here.
No carbides were found in the as-grown monocrystals (Fe-16%Al and Fe-17%Al) when no heat treatment was applied, consistent with the as-grown state of this sample.

The Fe-17%Al monocrystal (Table 1, row 17, Monocrystals) has a real Al content of 16.8 at.% (8.9 wt.-%) with impurities C 70 wt.ppm, Si 140 wt.ppm, and other elements Cu 50, Mo 90 (the nominal composition is 17 at.% Al).

Noticeable short-range ordering (K-state) develops in binary Fe-Al alloys with Al contents in the range 13–18 at.% at temperatures below 600 °C after solidification (highest degree at 250 °C); this applies to the Fe-17%Al alloy class but was not measured specifically for the as-grown monocrystal of this sample.
